question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(120,0.6),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=80).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,1.3\,$ $\,0.9032\,$ $\,0.9049\,$ $\,0.9066\,$
$\,1.4\,$ $\,0.9192\,$ $\,0.9207\,$ $\,0.9222\,$
$\,1.5\,$ $\,0.9332\,$ $\,0.9345\,$ $\,0.9357\,$
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,1.3\,$ $\,0.9147\,$ $\,0.9162\,$ $\,0.9177\,$
$\,1.4\,$ $\,0.9292\,$ $\,0.9306\,$ $\,0.9319\,$
$\,1.5\,$ $\,0.9418\,$ $\,0.9429\,$ $\,0.9441\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=120$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =120\cdot 0.6 \\  & =72 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =12\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =48 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(120)(0.6)=72
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(120)(0.6)(1-0.6)=28.8.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(72,28.8).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=80).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=80)≈P(79.5\le Y\le 80.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(79.5\le Y\le 80.5) & =P(\frac{79.5-72}{\sqrt{28.8}}\le Z\le \frac{80.5-72}{\sqrt{28.8}}) \\  & ≈P(1.40\le Z\le 1.58) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.58)-P(Z<1.40) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.58)-P(Z\le 1.40) \\  & =Φ(1.58)-Φ(1.40) \\  & =0.9429-0.9192 \\  & =0.0237\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=80)≈0.024.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0245.$
